filename: Deep Learning of Systematic Sea Ice Model Errors From Data Assimilation Increments.pdf
title: Deep Learning of Systematic Sea Ice Model Errors From Data Assimilation Increments
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
processes: sea ice concentration dynamics and thermodynamics
parameterization_target: sea ice concentration analysis increments (ΔSIC and category increments ΔSICN)
code_availability: All data for training each CNN are openly available (Gregory et al., 2023), along with auxiliary data such as the optimized CNN weights and standardization statistics. Python code to pre-process the input data and train the CNNs is also available at the same location: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7818178
testbed_rationale: The training and validation data comprising global sea ice and ocean states, tendencies, and corresponding DA analysis increments across 1982-2021 are openly available on Zenodo along with code. It provides an established benchmark for learning systematic Earth system model bias corrections.
pain_points: Data assimilation system was not originally tailored for ML training (e.g., only ensemble mean was readily saved rather than full 30-member ensembles).
Decoupling/disentangling sea ice errors from ocean or atmospheric errors in coupled models is challenging.
Preserving physical conservation laws (mass, heat, and salt budgets) when implementing offline-learned increments as parameterizations in a dynamical solver.
Scaling adjustments from 5-day DA increment intervals to sub-daily model timesteps.
Seasonal drop in predictability and signal variance during late summer melt months.
Non-stationarity of analysis increments over multidecadal timescales (variance increases over time).
extraction_notes: The paper focuses on offline evaluation of CNNs predicting DA increments of aggregate sea ice concentration and subgrid category concentrations, but expressly frames this as learning a parameterization for model bias correction.
